slides.title: DKIM2 IETF 127 - Main doc author slides

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: Slides not changing...

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Looks right to me

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: What is a subkey? The term doesn't appear in the draft

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: We're on slide 3, "Signing with multiple keys (and multiple hashes)"

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: @Jim: Might want to do that at the mic.

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: Finally moved to 3 after a long delay...

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: IANA Considerations: zzzzzzzzz...

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Someone remind me: Does DMARC relax only go up one label?

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: No

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Of course not. :-/

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: This is a new protocol. We should not be tied to bad practices from prior protocols.

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: With the tree walk, DMARC relax can go up seven labels

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Pete: "common ancestor" basically.

chat.author: Andrew Newton
chat.text: Maybe introduce the mail people to DCONN.

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: Inability to update a DNS record is pathetic, here's a nickel kid, get yourself a better DNS provider.

chat.author: Andrew Newton
chat.text: I agree there is some friction there, but DCONN is meant to solve this type of problem.

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: Many ESP customers are basically toddlers or infants in that scenario; they'd swallow the nickel

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Going back to the original DKIM work we've often made the assumption that the email and DNS people at corporations generally don't like each other very much, so one should rely minimally on the other.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: They're in different areas at the IETF, for what that's worth.  :-)

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: Actually I think Todd was saying they are unable

chat.author: Alex Brotman
chat.text: Not unable, but cumbersome at best

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: "they" is the ESP customer, not the ESP. Lots of Mom and Pop Shops that can't spell DNS, don't remember configuring it, and no longer speak to the granddaughter's ex-boyfriend  who set it up in the first place

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Difficulty is that all of these people you are describing are the people operating the ESP, not their customers (bakery shop owner, for example).

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: I also think it's been commonly accepted that new RRTYPEs are hard to use, even though they've become easier to register.

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: I'm with Tero, let those who can't make a DNS change stick with DKIM1 until they can...

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: We're not concerned that this will cause friction to adopt?

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: If a CRQC shows up one of these days, they'll need to update the DNS anyway.

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Mandatory if it's relevant

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: It's easy to see that it's not relevant, for example if the domains are equal

chat.author: Phillip Tao
chat.text: The from munging is only reversible for DKIM2 adopters. What's the story for non-adopters?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: I imagine DKIM1 rules apply.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: I'm still confused about the motivation for this. If a sender wants DKIM to break on modification, why can't that just be honored?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Because it's the recipient that decides whether it breaks, and if the signature succeeds, then it will pass.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: Rewriting the From header field will be invisible to many recipients unless the friendly-name is also munged. I doubt that would be required.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: Many (most?) MUAs don't display any email address to the recipient, munged or not. Only the friendly name.

chat.author: Phillip Tao
chat.text: How does this relate to Reply-To headers?

chat.author: Alexey Melnikov
chat.text: @Phillip: ask on mic?

chat.author: Phillip Tao
chat.text: If the From: is changed, but the original Reply-To is not, a user, on reply, may think they're replying to one sender but actually be applying to another, right?

chat.author: Andrew Newton
chat.text: What part of the charter is an issue?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: The beginning bit.  And the middle.  And most of the end.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text:
I'm tempted to punt on giving any advice about what MUAs should render, just as we did in DKIM itself.
We specified it more like an API, e.g., "Pass by $DOMAIN", and let the business logic take over from there.

chat.author: Alexey Melnikov
chat.text: Is this forcing MUAs to now understand DKIM2, where they didn't have to do this with DKIM1?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: @Andrew Newton "* There is a desire to maintain validation of a message's signing identifier across common transit and forwarding modifications. When a message goes through a re-posting, such as through a mailing list, the validation signature typically does not survive and cannot be recovered. Fixing this would permit a more robust evaluation of the message."

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: We do seem to be talking a lot about maybe expanding DKIM2's scope well into MUA space.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: FWIW: Null recipes do strike me as good reason to munge From. It's the minor change recipe that makes me sad.

chat.author: Andrew Newton
chat.text: I have a stupid question, what is "client" in this case?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Time check: Just under an hour remaining.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text:
https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftthreatprotectionblog/strengthening-email-ecosystem-outlook’s-new-requirements-for-high%E2%80%90volume-senders/4399730



Does publishing a strict DMARC policy (p=reject) offer better security?


Absolutely, once your legitimate sources are aligned, p=reject is the most effective at thwarting domain spoofing. We advise moving gradually (none → quarantine → reject) to avoid unintended mail loss.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: yeah, but who sees the actual domain name these days

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: The only reason everyone does not have p=reject is likely laziness, not intent. Even MS is encouraging everyone to p=reject. They will equally recommend "donotmodify" (or to dis-recommend "canmodify") for everyone.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: BIMI talked a year or two ago about re-attempting a BoF, but nothing came of it.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: BIMI's first BoF was disasterous.

chat.author: Phillip Tao
chat.text: If this leads to more body modification (because it's now "safe" to do), I feel like you almost need to give some MUA guidance. Currently, email generally has a single provenance. If email messages now have multiple authors for various bits of content, that changes the nature, and I don't know what I should do with that.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: That's how I recall it as well.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: (@Jim)

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: @Pete I'm lazy, but that's not why I don't have p=reject.

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: Avoding the need for a recipe for BIMI makes sense to me, not signing them can be at least a BCP.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: I haven't done the minutes from the last interim yet.  I suspect the action item to do a CFA for Bron's A-R document is in there.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: I'll mark it as a candidate for this WE.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: WG*

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: DMARC WG is talking about winding down

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: Is updating DMARC in charter for DKIM?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: @Jim Fenton You (and I) are I believe in a tiny end of an asymptote.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: @Pete Yes, we're the long tail.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: @Todd Herr "This working group will also liaise with the DMARC working group on adding its specification as a new recognized authentication mechanism. If the DMARC working group has concluded by that time, this working group can undertake that update in coordination with the responsible Area Directors."

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: (applause)

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: @Pete - Thanks

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Are remote people hearing clipping from Wei's audio?

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Not really

chat.author: Alex Brotman
chat.text: Not me

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: OK it's in the room, thanks.

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: Well, since the DNS is immutable, those DMARC recod changes can't happen. :-)

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Time check: 45 minutes.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: Victor: it's unevenly mutable.  SOME people can do any changes and rotate things frequently, some have no ability to do much at all.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Particularly, customers of commercial email sending services (i.e., advertisers, et. al.) have scant little ability to update their DNS.

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: The ":-)" was intended to not elicit serious responses.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Just assuring that it was not snark implying that the people saying so were somehow making something up.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: My recollection is that owners of DNS in places like banks and governments are reticent to let anyone touch their stuff.

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: @Murray - Your recollection matches my experience

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: But I've also had contrary experiences, like at my current employer who very much say "You want it changed, go change it.  Config files are over there."

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: "You break it, you bought it."

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: CanModifyIfYouWant

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: WeKnowYouWillAnyway

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: PleaseModify

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: CanModifyButBeGentle

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Someone close the door?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: (screams in draft-kucherawy-dkim-transform)

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: The chairs are likely to ask "who plans to implement this, both on the sending side and on the receiving side?"

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Time check: 30 minutes.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: transform is a subset of recipes but yeah, basically that!

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: A fully general bodywrap is likely to be a problem: If I have a plain text message, I can pretty straightforwardly replace a body by dorking with the Content-Type.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: I like the idea of "original mail" as the middle part, required to still pass its own DKIM signature.

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: It still goes to the envelope sender...

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text:
Time check: 10 minutes.
I have one short chair/AOB item.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: We really seem to have a conflict of requirements here.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Seems so.

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Why not both?

chat.author: Hans-Jörg Happel
chat.text: DKIMARC

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: (hissing noise)

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: DMARKIM

chat.author: Richard Clayton
chat.text: DARK

chat.author: Viktor Dukhovni
chat.text: Yes, and I do think that multiple requirement profiles are viable, with some care.

chat.author: Jim Fenton
chat.text: When ADSP was made historic, did that require WG charter?
